indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wavering Conservatives are coaxed out of their party into the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot make up their mind is irresolute: a plain synonym for wavering.

indicators.note: oddly tells us to take the odd-numbered letters of the word indulged

explanation.surface: A pampered person with no job, living a life of ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers with no job are said to be idle, a common synonym for out of work.

clue.text: Bother doctor initially massaging a part

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig or falsify them

indicators.note: initially signals the opening letter of the word massaging

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A doctor fussing over a massage of one bit of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but works as a verb meaning to fix or falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a tiresome, long-winded fuss, so it is a kind of bother or hassle.

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, so we want a word sounding like the synonym

parts.note: displays or spectacles are sights

explanation.surface: Something that puts on a show for the people watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to place or position it, so sites works as a verb meaning installs.

clue.text: Cattle confused about front of iron grid

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
confused means mixed up, so the letters of cattle are jumbled
front of signals the first letter of the word iron

explanation.surface: Muddled cattle wander round an iron grid, perhaps a cattle grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns CATTLE into LATTCE, and 'about' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework of strips, essentially a grid or trellis.

clue.text: Nearly ripped and torn apart by deluge

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: ripped means torn
rent is an old past tense of rend, meaning torn apart

explanation.surface: Clothes almost ripped and shredded in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the N from TORN, leaving TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water, much like a deluge or flood.

clue.text: Instrument with hot amp ends covering Queen

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot on taps

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the outer letters enclose the other piece
ends signals the first and last letters of the word amp

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument plugged into a hot amplifier while playing for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts the letters A and P around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp is a stringed musical instrument plucked with the fingers.

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the article goes around the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a fabrication is a lie

explanation.surface: A disgusting newspaper article that is full of made-up stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alien to one's nature is foreign and so distasteful or repugnant, as in cruelty being alien to her.

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walking at the end of a long trek, utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' reads as British slang for exhausted, fitting the walker, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means going on foot rather than riding, from Latin pes, foot.

explanation.surface: Is it justified to flee? The clue asks and then answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is the slang phrase for running off; as one word it is short for legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is informal shorthand for legitimate, meaning lawful or justified.

indicators.note: pottering about means moving aimlessly here and there, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dreads retirement and the prospect of pottering around all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Being terrified is being greatly frightened, a stronger form of alarmed.

clue.text: Thankless person kept by tax-paying ratepayers

indicators.note: kept by means held within, so the answer sits inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A council supported by local taxpayers who shows no gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who fails to show thanks.

clue.text: Positive sign of excitement going after gold

indicators.note: going after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
spice is zest or excitement

explanation.surface: A thrill of excitement on chasing after gold, taken as a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen, originally a sign read from the flight of birds, here a favourable one.

indicators.note: putting out means removing, so one piece is taken out of the other

parts.note: a virtuoso is a genius at their art
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A band whose star performer releases a solo single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' looks like releasing a record but means removing the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification group ranking above species.

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sneer at paid celebrities behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched in the sense of vile or contemptible matches despicable.

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the synonym is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book or work; the 's stands for is
the crossword compiler is I, so compiler's is I have, shortened

explanation.surface: A setter whose work has been turned down is feeling sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TOME into EMOT; 'compiler' is the setter speaking of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy subject stirs strong feeling, which is what an emotive one does.

clue.text: Right to enter artist's Salon opening

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

indicators.note: opening signals the first letter of the word Salon

explanation.surface: A painter is granted entry to the Paris Salon on its opening day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress means the act or right of going in, the opposite of egress.

clue.text: Judas, corrupt one with cunning turned back

indicators.note: turned back means read in reverse, applying to the whole run of pieces

parts.note: to rot is to corrupt or decay
I is the Roman numeral one
art can mean cunning or craft, as in artful

explanation.surface: A corrupt and crafty person who turned his back on his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses ROTIART as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for any betrayer.

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer swapping partners announces a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: When facts transpire they emerge or become known, which is to come out.

clue.text: Promised to fix shelf in vacant pad

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shelf goes within the other piece
vacant means emptied, so only the outer letters of pad remain

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Someone vowed to put up a shelf in an empty flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge is to give one's word, so pledged is a synonym of vowed.

clue.text: Game over then pitch second over

indicators.note: the second over means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over
to lob is to pitch or throw
to second someone is to back them, so second can mean aid

explanation.surface: A cricket match: another over, then a bowl, then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'over' reverses OLOBAID. An over in cricket is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a spool is spun on a string between two sticks.

indicators.note: almost finished means stopping short of the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a grenade is a small bomb
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A bomb nearly done, ready to wreck a developed nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Ships' passage stopped by empty Ganges

definitions.note: the clue has a possessive; the plural noun means ships, the oared vessels

indicators.note: stopped by means blocked by, so the passage sits between the other letters
empty means hollowed out, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: A ships' route on the river is blocked where the Ganges runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on 'Ships'' is surface dressing; galleys are both oared ships and ships' kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleys were long low vessels rowed by oars, a type of ship.

indicators.note: after means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
one who is separate is alone, or lone

explanation.surface: A carbon copy is a separate item made afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon copy' reads as one phrase, but carbon gives C and copy alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact genetic duplicate, hence any copy.

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Saying no before agreeing to a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal here is softwood timber, not an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, so it is to declare one's view.

clue.text: Insists everybody say, is taking English

parts.note: everybody means all
e.g. means for example, which say also signals
is shortened to an apostrophe S

explanation.surface: Everyone claims that some point is taken in English lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, so to insist it is so.

clue.text: Crack's seen around top of short pants

indicators.note: seen around means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: a crack is a gap; the 's makes it plural

indicators.note: top of signals the first letter of the word short

explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like a noun for trousers but is the verb, breathes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pants is breathing in short gasps, so pants and gasps are verb synonyms.

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: the gut is the stomach

explanation.surface: A big belly from eating too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, so an excess or surplus.

parts.note: brims are edges or borders
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A butterfly trailing coloured edges on its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a common yellow butterfly of Europe.

clue.text: Start to spin top, showing expertise

indicators.note: start to signals the opening letter of the word spin

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: Spinning a toy top shows real dexterity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like the spinning toy but is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill is ability or proficiency, a synonym of expertise.

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The first woman was right all along.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, as in ever hopeful, so it is always.

clue.text: Regular felons one dispatched having time inside

parts.note: cons are convicts, felons
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: inside means within, so the time letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: dispatched means sent

explanation.surface: Habitual criminals, one sent away to do time inside prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like prison slang but places T within SENT, making STENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consistent is steady and unvarying, which is regular.
